hero.secondary: Which of these problems sounds like yours?

problems.title: You have an idea, but nothing is built yet
problems.agitate: Every month without a product is a month handed to your competitors. And a wrong technical choice at the start costs you for years: an app to rewrite, payments that fail, a team blocked by its own architecture.
fixes: I start from your real need and scope a first useful version
I design the architecture: API, database, web and mobile apps
I build what makes the product live: payments, notifications, real time
I publish to the stores and ship to production, with the tests

proofs.name: Utando
proofs.text: Logistics platform designed from scratch: Node.js / Fastify API on PostgreSQL, 3 Expo apps and a React back office, MTN MoMo and Orange Money payments, a payouts ledger, background jobs and geolocation.

proofs.name: Cooltchop
proofs.text: Food delivery built end to end: the PHP / Slim API, the React Native app and the web version. Over 5,000 downloads on Google Play.

proofs.name: Snow Volican
proofs.text: Events platform built alone: FastAPI on PostgreSQL, React front end, Stripe payments, Sentry on front and back end.

next.label: Your product exists, but it keeps breaking?

problems.title: Your app breaks in production
problems.agitate: Every release becomes a gamble. Payment fails on a Friday night, your customers notice before you do, and the team spends the week fighting fires instead of moving forward.
fixes: End-to-end tests on the paths that bring money: signup, cart, payment
Docker images built by GitHub Actions, identical in test and production
A release checked before the switch, with instant rollback
Sentry on front end and back end, to see the error before the customer does

proofs.name: Adsquid
proofs.text: 344 Playwright tests on signup, cart and Stripe / PayPal payment. 10 production releases with blue-green deploys and instant rollback.

proofs.name: Snow Volican
proofs.text: Zero-downtime deploys: several instances behind Nginx, health checks, one instance updated at a time, triggered by GitHub Actions.

proofs.name: Real-estate CRM
proofs.text: 290 test files covering login, two-factor authentication, roles and client identity checks.

next.label: The code is there, but nobody understands it?

problems.title: You inherited code nobody understands
problems.agitate: Every change breaks something else. The original developer is gone, the announced migration was never really done, and your roadmap moves at the pace of regressions.
fixes: I audit what exists: what works, what breaks, what's missing
I turn the audit into a migration plan in small, verifiable steps
I put tests in place as a safety net before touching the core
Every fixed bug becomes an automatic rule so it never comes back

proofs.name: Adsquid
proofs.text: Audited 10 modules, 563 columns and 262 business rules: only 9 columns were actually migrated. The audit became the migration plan to Payload CMS and Next.js on PostgreSQL.

proofs.name: Epiltech
proofs.text: Shop and training courses migrated from Prisma to Payload on PostgreSQL, with the whole infrastructure self-hosted on Docker Compose and daily backups.

problems.title: Your users wait, then leave
problems.agitate: Three seconds too many, a network drop, a stuttering screen: users don't complain, they uninstall. And you never find out.
fixes: I measure before and after every fix, to prove the gain
I cut what the app redraws and what it downloads
I design for unstable networks and small phones
I set up real time properly: WebRTC, sockets, STOMP

proofs.name: StackZ and One2All TV
proofs.meta: Sole developer of the TV and mobile apps
proofs.text: A remote-control move redraws 2 cards instead of about 14, measured with Flashlight. WebRTC live video, STOMP real time, Picture-in-Picture, published on 3 stores.

proofs.name: Docta
proofs.text: Flutter app with real-time chat over sockets and a map of nearby practitioners.

next.label: And when your messages don't arrive?

problems.title: Your notifications don't arrive, or they annoy
problems.agitate: A driver misses a ride, a payment is confirmed without anyone knowing, or the app sends so many messages that your users turn everything off.
fixes: Reliable push notifications on Android and iOS
Android channels and per-type preferences
Scheduled reminders with a frequency cap
Email and calendar when push isn't the right channel

proofs.name: Utando
proofs.text: Push on the driver, partner and traveler apps and the back office, with Android notification channels.

proofs.name: Karreer
proofs.text: Push notifications with cron-scheduled reminders and a frequency cap, so users are never flooded.

proofs.name: Real-estate CRM
proofs.text: Scheduled visits with email notifications and a calendar invite, and a first contact required within 4 hours for every lead.
